name: The Detective's Casebook
description: Poe's first sleuth, Holmes on his foggy streets, Christie's clever puzzles and the hard-boiled eye of America: how the mystery story was invented and spread.

checkpoints.name: The first detectives
checkpoints.note: Poe's Paris sleuth Dupin gave crime fiction its pattern: a baffling crime, a clever outsider and a surprising explanation, and Collins soon extended it to a full novel.

checkpoints.name: Holmes arrives
checkpoints.note: A Scottish doctor created Sherlock Holmes in 1887, and the Strand Magazine made him a worldwide celebrity, while Christie was born.

checkpoints.name: The golden age
checkpoints.note: In Britain Christie perfected the puzzle with a closed circle of suspects, while American writers such as Hammett and Chandler took the detective into the city streets.

checkpoints.name: Mystery goes global
checkpoints.note: Spies, boy detectives in Tokyo, a Swedish hacker and a Paris thriller show how the mystery spread to every corner of popular culture.
